apps.name: Jellyfin
apps.description: Jellyfin web client in the kiosk browser, pointed at the media server on the rack.

apps.name: YouTube
apps.user_agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux i686) AppleWebKit/534.24 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/11.0.696.77 Large Screen Safari/534.24 GoogleTV/092754
apps.description: YouTube's TV interface (big tiles, remote and pad friendly) in the kiosk browser.

apps.name: AirPlay
apps.description: AirPlay screen mirroring from a phone or Mac, using UxPlay. Installing the packages needs root (asks for the PIN). Uninstalling removes the tile and leaves the shared packages installed.
install: sudo apt install -y uxplay avahi-daemon gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad gstreamer1.0-plugins-good gstreamer1.0-libav python3-gi gir1.2-gtk-3.0

apps.name: Steam Link
apps.description: Streams games from the Windows PC. Installing the package needs root.

apps.name: Kodi
apps.description: The full Kodi media center, started on its own home with the TV remote kept by Lumen. Installing and uninstalling need the PIN. Uninstalling keeps ~/.kodi (library, add-ons, settings, game saves) and ~/roms. RetroArch is the game player now; Kodi's RetroPlayer is no longer set up.
install: sudo apt install -y kodi kodi-game-libretro kodi-inputstream-adaptive libretro-mgba libretro-gambatte libretro-desmume kodi-repository-kodi
uninstall: sudo apt remove -y kodi kodi-game-libretro kodi-inputstream-adaptive libretro-mgba libretro-gambatte libretro-desmume kodi-repository-kodi kodi-visualization-spectrum

apps.name: Spotify
apps.description: Spotify's web player in the kiosk browser with Widevine for playback. It shows up as a Spotify Connect device your phone can pick. Installing needs root (asks for the PIN) to add the Widevine package. Lyrics are in Spotify's own player. Keeps playing when you go Home.
apps.notes: Signing in needs a keyboard once; the login is then kept. The remote's arrows move a green focus ring, OK opens an album or playlist and plays a song; the lyrics button is in the player bar. Your phone can also pick it as a Connect device.

apps.name: Spotify Connect
apps.description: Spotify's official headless Connect receiver (Soloist). This box becomes a speaker your phone can pick in Spotify. It has no tile and no screen, and it keeps playing whatever Lumen shows. It needs Spotify Premium and your own Soloist API key.
apps.notes: Soloist is downloaded from Spotify onto this box. It is covered by Spotify's terms, not Lumen's licence, and Lumen never redistributes it. Spotify's terms don't clearly cover using Soloist through third-party tools like Lumen, and Spotify can change or withdraw it at any time. Use at your own risk. Get your own key from Spotify's developer site (Soloist API Key page, https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/soloist); a Premium account is needed to create it. After installing, set the key over SSH: sh ~/lumen-tv/session/lumen-soloist set-key, then paste it (it is not echoed). The device name is this box's hostname. Builds expire after 90 days, so Lumen re-downloads it weekly. Uninstalling keeps your key.

apps.name: RetroArch
apps.description: The game player: Game Boy, Game Boy Color, Game Boy Advance and Nintendo DS through mGBA, Gambatte and melonDS. Large download (about 400 MB plus the KDE runtime). Uninstalling keeps your saves and ~/roms.
apps.notes: Put ROMs in ~/roms (gb, gba, nds) and pick Load Content in RetroArch. Cores are downloaded at install time from the libretro nightly builds. It runs through Xwayland on purpose: native Wayland falls back to software rendering. Saves live in ~/.var/app/org.libretro.RetroArch.
install: set -e; T=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT; D=~/.var/app/org.libretro.RetroArch/config/retroarch/cores; mkdir -p "$D"; for c in mgba gambatte melonds; do curl -fsSL -o "$T/$c.zip" "https://buildbot.libretro.com/nightly/linux/aarch64/latest/${c}_libretro.so.zip"; python3 -c 'import sys,zipfile; zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]).extractall(sys.argv[2])' "$T/$c.zip" "$D"; done

apps.name: Moonlight
apps.description: Streams games from a PC running Sunshine or GeForce Experience. The Pi 5 has no hardware H.264 decoding, so high resolutions and frame rates may stutter.
apps.notes: Pairing with the PC needs a PIN typed once, so a keyboard or mouse is needed the first time.

apps.name: chiaki-ng
apps.description: Remote Play for PlayStation 4 and 5 consoles. Heavy (about 230 MB download). Experimental on the Pi: not yet checked on the TV, so it may not run well or at all.
apps.notes: Needs a PSN sign-in and console pairing once, with a keyboard.

apps.name: VLC
apps.description: Plays video and audio files and network streams. The interface is a desktop one, so it is best driven with a keyboard or mouse.
apps.notes: Open files from ~/ or a network stream address. Remote and pad navigation is limited.

apps.name: Audiobookshelf
apps.description: Audiobookshelf web client in the kiosk browser, pointed at the audiobook server on the rack. Keeps playing when you go Home.
apps.notes: Sign in with a keyboard once; the login is then kept.

apps.name: Twitch
apps.description: Twitch's website in the kiosk browser. It has no TV interface, so navigating with the remote may be awkward. Not yet checked on the TV.
